label: <DEL> delimiter step, or input a/r in the original phase
explanation: Fires almost only on input steps, with nearly nothing in the copy phase (0.2% of mass). About 44% of mass is on the <DEL> delimiter step, which fires in 34% of sequences. Most of the rest is on original-phase inputs of a (44% rate when a is input, 43% of mass), r (19% rate) and o (7%). The largest activations are a near the start of the sequence, especially runs of repeated a (a a a builds toward the max); a at orig_idx <= 3 is active 87% of the time. a later in the sequence and r are weaker. Delimiter activations are moderate (mostly 0.1-0.45 of max). I could not find what decides whether <DEL> fires: whether a appears in the original, the digit count and L each shift the rate only a little. It essentially never fires on other letters or digits, or on copy-phase steps. The predicate covers 93% of activation mass, but precision is about 0.41, mainly because of <DEL> steps that do not fire and late a/r inputs.
